name: SIRUP
title: Spatial Immune Receptor Utilities Package
description: A consolidated toolkit for long-read spatial immune receptor sequencing. SIRUP takes demultiplexed reads from the companion 'RRAD' package and runs an end-to-end IgBLAST and pRESTO pipeline to produce AIRR-style rearrangement tables with spatial IDs and coordinates. It also provides Visium HD barcode mapping, clonal summaries, tree plotting, polygon annotation, and spatial statistics.

requirements.imports: airrblast, alakazam, cli, cowplot, data.table, dowser, dplyr, ggplot2, ggtree, grDevices, grid, igraph, jsonlite, kedd, KernSmooth, magrittr, Matrix, methods, parallel, patchwork, pbapply, RANN, rlang, scales, SeuratObject, sf, shiny, spdep, stats, stringr, tibble, tidyr, tools, utils
requirements.suggests: airr, ape, arrow, BiocNeighbors, knitr, nabor, pals, qpdf, rgl, rmarkdown, scoper, Seurat, shazam, spatstat.explore, spatstat.geom, spatstat.random, testthat (>= 3.0.0), withr

pages.title: Get started with SIRUP
pages.summary: Build a SIRUP object from example data, plot receptors on the tissue, draw a region, and measure clonal dominance in it.

pages.title: Process demultiplexed reads
pages.summary: Turn demultiplexed long-read data into an AIRR table of consensus receptor sequences with one spatial ID for each sequence.

pages.title: Annotate tissue ROIs and analyze local clonal structure
pages.summary: Draw tissue regions, attach them to a SIRUP object, and measure clonal dominance, clonal diversity, and gene expression in each region.

pages.title: Infer clones and lineage trees in situ
pages.summary: Call clones, reconstruct germlines, build lineage trees with Dowser, and show each tree next to its spots on the tissue.

pages.title: Analyze multiple spatial sections and bulk BCR-seq
pages.summary: Put several tissue sections, bulk AIRR-seq, and blood samples in one SIRUP object, and follow clones between them.

pages.title: How the SIRUP object works
pages.summary: Learn the five parts of a SIRUP object, the rules that SIRUP checks, and the functions that change the object.

pages.title: Choose the right spatial statistic for your question
pages.summary: Pick a spatial statistic by the question you ask: clustering, co-variation, nearness of two spot types, or the spread of a clone.

pages.title: Use QuPath annotations to define ROIs
pages.summary: Export germinal center outlines from QuPath as GeoJSON and add them to a SIRUP object as polygons, then check how the spots and the outlines line up.

pages.title: Use SIRUP with your LLM agent
pages.summary: Give an LLM agent such as Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity the SIRUP skill or the llms files, and work with it on spatial receptor data.
